newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Sellers send Australian stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sellers send Australian stocks to lower close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2474 -19 US 30yr cl 6.58 +0.03
10yrbond futs 92.550 -0.130 Gold NY 345.55 Lon fix 345.55
*Stocks end lower as profit-takers cash in, bonds slide with future-linked selling. No impact from Deng death. Volume 412.54 million, A$935.36 million, 1,125 traded, 333 steady, 361 up, 431 down.
A combination of a battered bond market and profit-taking after its recent record breaking run pushed the Australian share market to a lower close on Thursday.
The death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping had no impact on the local market, traders said.
"It was nothing to be concerned about. It was more curiosity value than anything else," said a Sydney-based dealer.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 14.7 points lower at 2,476.3.
The March share price index futures contract was 19 points lower at 2,474, a 2.3 point discount to the underlying index.
China-related stocks ended mixed in mostly thin trade after the announcement of Deng's death.
Brokers noted that trading in that sector of the market was usually choppy and illiquid with over half of the companies making up the Australian Stock Exchange's Asian index untraded on the day.

China Construction Holdings eased four cents to 85 cents while OLS Asia Holdings ended unchanged at 80 cents, as did Jardine Fleming China Region at 61 cents while NMFM Asia Investments lost a cent to close at 87 cents.

Profit taking in the big banks, particularly in Commonwealth Bank of Australia and National Australia Bank which both lost over 1.5 percent to A$13.33 and A$16.64 respectively, pressured the leaders right from the start.
An afternoon slide in bond futures then exacerbated softer sentiment on the day, generating selling in the March SPI contract that flowed into the underlying markets.

"The futures have been knocked about a bit today," said dealer Jamie Spiteri of Shaw Stockbroking, noting that the underlying market's showing had been a continuation of the slide started on Wednesday afternoon.

"In the last hour of trading yesterday, our market was on a downward slide and that has continued as the day's gone on here. Really, this is the aftermath of what has been a pretty solid couple of weeks, there is no specific reason for it."
Results remained the focus with plenty reported today.
Shares of Burns Philp and Co ended five cents lower at A$2.09 after the food ingredients group reported a 17.6 percent rise in first half net profit to A$48.2 million.
Construction group Leighton lost 15 cents to A$5.70 despite an 18 percent higher first half net profit of A$32.04 million and 42 percent higher dividend.

Qantas Airways reported a 2.4 percent higher first half net profit of A$151.6 million. Its shares closed four cents higher at A$2.46 after reaching A$2.48, their highest level since listing in July 1995.
Sydney Harbour Casino shares topped turnover with 27.5 million shares traded, the bulk of it in two lines specialled through Merrill Lynch. Its shares closed six cents lower at A$2.29.
Mineral sands, tin and copper miner RGC Ltd posted a four percent lower first half net profit of A$32.32 million. Its shares slumped 27.6 cents to close at A$5.25.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.44 percent, well up on Wednesday's 7.30 percent levels.
The Australian dollar kept a grip on 1/2 cent of offshore gains late Thursday but was finding it hard to extend the rally into safer territory atop 77 cents.
Traders said heavy buying, some options related and some from a U.K. corporate, had soaked up impressive amounts of sales and squeezed the currency up from US$0.7635 support.
By 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the local dollar had found a temporary ceiling at US$0.7685/90 from an early US$0.7676/81, having bounced from US$0.7637/42 late here Wednesday.
